text:
Seth Jones has 26 points in 25 games, and that pace would be new territory for him. A season ago he managed 32 in 52. The difference is the power play: 16 of his points have come with the extra man, and he's playing 24:33 a night.

What makes this convincing is that little of it looks lucky. The Panthers' finishing with him on the ice is right about where the chances say it should be, and at even strength they take 54.85% of the shot attempts with him out there. His own goals, three on 3.83 expected, are ordinary for a defenseman. The questions are the old ones. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season had only 30% of his exits keeping the puck, though he was hard to beat at his own blue line, stopping 18% of entries. Our numbers project 69 points, which would be a career year for the Stanley Cup winner.
headline: Seth Jones is scoring like he never has
